findings.message: This only fixes one case of last round's stale-mark finding. upsertSpecProposal moves `synced_commit_at` only when the caller passes `committedAt`, and that input is optional on `sync_proposal` (mcp.ts:79). The round-3 finding named the `sync_proposal` tool as a writer, but its existing callers, the 008 CI credentials and specclaw, still send no commit time. Their writes therefore change title, phase and tasks without moving the mark. The README now says the mark is 'set by every writer that knows its commit time', but nothing makes a writer give that time. The new test covers only the syncSpecclaw/bin path, which is the one variant that passes it. Fix: make `committedAt` required for `source: "specclaw"` writes through sync_proposal, or have the push refuse (flag `needsReview`) any proposal whose last specclaw write recorded no mark. Add `sync_proposal` without `committedAt` as a row in the AC-8 variant table, beside the self-sync row.
findings.scenario: At 12:30, CI calls sync_proposal {key:'FLT-102', title:'Import v2', …} with no committedAt, so FLT-102's mark stays at its 09:00 push. A developer then pushes sync_specclaw from a 12:25 commit with title 'Import'. The stale gate compares 09:00 < 12:25, accepts the push and overwrites the 12:30 title.

findings.message: `defaultBranch` falls back to "main" when it is left out. That default now decides which pushes may update every change. Relinking (for example, changing the URL) without restating the branch quietly resets a stored `master` or `trunk` to `main`. Fix: on relink, keep the stored `repo_default_ref` when no branch is given. When there is nothing stored yet, require the branch or ask for it.
findings.scenario: CON is linked with defaultBranch 'trunk'. A PM runs link_project_repo {projectKey:'CON', repoUrl:'https://github.com/example/portal-new'}, and repo_default_ref becomes 'main'. Pushes from trunk now cover only a change named 'trunk' and come back flagged nomatch. If an old 'main' branch still exists, its pushes cover every change.

findings.message: `hasCredentials` refuses any `scheme://user@` URL. That includes `ssh://git@github.com/org/repo`, which names only an SSH user. The comment in repo-url.ts says an SSH user is accepted, but that holds only for the scp form. Fix: refuse a userinfo only when it holds a ':' secret, or when the scheme is http(s).
findings.scenario: A PM links 'ssh://git@github.com/example/portal' and gets 'remove the user name or token from the repo URL', although the URL holds no secret.

findings.message: The README says 'One push is one transaction under the project's row lock'. pushSpecclaw now runs applyPush twice: a rolled-back preview transaction that decides between unchanged and apply, then a separate `applied` transaction. Fix the wording so it matches the two-transaction flow, or merge the decision into one transaction.

This round fixed the bare-transaction blocker by deleting the mark update for unchanged records, so the stale-mark fix now regresses. The mark moves only inside upsertSpecProposal, which runs only for rows that change. A push or a 039 self-sync whose record already matches the stored row leaves `synced_commit_at` at the older commit. A later push from a commit between the two then passes the stale gate. The same gap is in sync/import.ts, which calls syncProposal only for changed rows. The test hides this: its expected mark was changed from 10:00 to 09:00. Fix: inside the audited service transaction (`applied`, or a small defineService mark step), advance the mark for every record the push covered, unchanged ones included, and do the same for the self-sync. Add a variant test: an unchanged push from a newer commit, then an older commit with different content, which must be skipped as stale.
findings.scenario: FLT-102 was last written from commit A (09:00, title 'X'), so the mark is 09:00. Main commit C (09:30) renamed it to 'Y'. Main commit B (10:00) reverted the title to 'X'. B is pushed: unchanged, mark stays 09:00. A delayed push of C (09:30 > 09:00) passes the gate and writes the reverted title 'Y' over main's current state.
